sections.label: Healthier SG strategy and engagement
sections.summary: Healthier SG is a reform shifting care to preventive, community-based care, and MOH engaged over 6,000 public members and 1,000 healthcare professionals.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: And if we can replicate that whole effort in our fight against debilitating chronic illnesses, especially those that come with ageing, then we would have made a big difference in the coming 10 years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: And that is why we developed the Healthier SG strategy, which I announced in the Committee of Supply (COS) earlier this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: It is a fundamental re-orientation and reform of our healthcare system, focus on preventive care instead of curative care, emphasise on health instead of sickness, to shift the centre of gravity of care away from hospitals, into the community, to rely less on doctors for health, but to depend on communities, our families and ourselves – and live up to the name of Ministry of Health (MOH), not Ministry of Sickness.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: During COS, I said that we would seek the inputs of stakeholders, as we flesh out our proposals, and then we will come back to Parliament again.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: And since then, MOH engaged more than 6,000 members of the public, including 1,000 healthcare professionals.

sections.label: Designing system with useful inputs
sections.summary: The process aims to design the system right, and useful inputs were incorporated in the White Paper.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: It is an important process to make sure that we design the system right.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: And we got many useful inputs, which we have tried our best to incorporate in this White Paper.

sections.label: National enrolment exercise start
sections.summary: The national enrolment exercise begins in the second half of 2023, starting with residents aged 60 and above.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: And once the first three components are ready, we embark on the fourth, which is the national enrolment exercise.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: And this will commence in the second half of 2023 next year, starting with residents aged 60 and above.

sections.label: NKF dialysis patient numbers
sections.summary: At the National Kidney Foundation, six more patients in Singapore require dialysis every day.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: I visited the National Kidney Foundation (NKF) recently.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: They told me that every day, six more patients in Singapore require dialysis  – every day, six more.

sections.label: Fully funded preventive care
sections.summary: Enrolled residents get fully funded annual check-ins, vaccinations, and screenings for three chronic conditions and three cancers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The second area of support is that once you are enrolled with a family doctor, the Government will fully fund the most important aspects of preventive care.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Hence, annual preventive care check-ins with your family doctor, nationally recommended vaccinations, such as influenza and pneumococcal vaccinations and health screenings will be free.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Health screenings will include three very common chronic conditions – type 2 diabetes, hypertension and hyperlipidaemia, and three cancers: breast, cervical and colorectal.

sections.label: MediSave chronic illness co-payment
sections.summary: Residents using MediSave for chronic illness treatment no longer need to co-pay 15% of the bill in cash.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The third way to support residents – if you are using MediSave to pay for the treatment of your chronic illness, you are no longer required to co-pay 15% of the bill using cash.

sections.label: CHAS subsidy tier for chronic drugs
sections.summary: An additional CHAS subsidy tier for common chronic drugs and drug price limits will be introduced to level the price difference.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: To help residents anchor with a family doctor of their choice, we intend to level this price difference, by introducing an additional subsidy tier to Community Health Assist Scheme (CHAS) for common chronic drugs and also set drug price limits.

sections.label: Removing drug price difference
sections.summary: Drug prices cannot be equalised to the last cent, but the difference will be substantively removed for Healthier SG enrollees.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: There is a technical reason, but we will not be able to equalise the price down to the last cent.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: But we will substantively remove the current difference in drug prices between the two for individuals enrolled in Heathier SG.

sections.label: Healthpoints for healthy lifestyle
sections.summary: Healthpoints will be awarded to encourage residents to adopt and sustain a healthy lifestyle.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Sixth, we will award Healthpoints to help encourage residents to adopt and sustain a healthy lifestyle.

sections.label: Annual service fee for GPs
sections.summary: MOH will extend an annual service fee payment for each resident who enrols with them.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: MOH will, therefore, extend an annual service fee payment for each resident who enrol with them.

sections.label: Set up cost and service fees
sections.summary: Set up cost is estimated at over $1 billion over three to four years, plus about $400 million per year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: We need new IT systems, ground support capabilities, give GPs one-time support for the necessary IT enhancements and capability-building to bring them on board.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: So, we estimate a set up cost of over $1 billion over the next three to four years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: This includes all the support measures for residents I talked about earlier and the annual service fee for GPs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: This is estimated to be another $400 million per year.

sections.label: National annual medical bill growth
sections.summary: The annual medical bill for the whole nation is expected to almost multiply threefold to $60 billion in 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: This is the annual medical bill for the whole nation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: We are expecting it to almost multiply threefold, in the coming 10 years, to $60 billion in 2030.

sections.label: Dedicated family doctor for all
sections.summary: Every Singaporean should visit a dedicated family doctor or clinic.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The key components are described below: First, and most importantly, we need to ensure that every Singaporean visits a dedicated family doctor or clinic.

sections.label: Increased preventive care subsidies
sections.summary: The Government will increase subsidies for preventive care.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Second, the Government will increase subsidies for preventive care.

sections.label: Healthier SG chronic illness and rewards
sections.summary: Healthier SG removes cash co-payment for chronic illness treatment and uses the Healthy 365 app to expand healthy lifestyle rewards.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Under the Healthier SG system, we will do away with the cash co-payment for the treatment of chronic illnesses.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Fourth, we will also utilise the Healthy 365 app to expand the scope of rewards for adopting a healthy lifestyle.

sections.label: Population health and healthy longevity
sections.summary: Population health brings healthcare, social support, societal habits and personal responsibility together, aiming for healthy longevity.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The traditional understanding of healthcare comprises primary and acute care – ICUs, hospitals, clinics.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: But there is also the concept of population health where healthcare, social support systems and societal habits – plus personal responsibility – come together to make a population healthy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: There is a similar concept in Chinese medicine.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: It is well summarised by Tang Dynasty doctor Sun Simiao (孙思邈) who said, "上医医国, 中医医人, 下医医病".

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: If all of us come together to make Healthier SG work, we will progress towards the holy grail of healthcare – healthy longevity.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: That is when the number of years we can live healthily approximates the number of years we can live biologically.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Members will be glad to know that Parliament Sittings can be part of the Healthier SG range of activities as well.

sections.label: Subsidising screenings and chronic disease care
sections.summary: Nationally recommended screenings and vaccinations will be fully subsidised, removing cash co-payment for chronic disease treatment under a family doctor.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: The less well-off might well be affected the most.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: So, it is an important step to fully subsidise nationally recommended screenings and vaccinations for Singaporeans, to remove the need for cash co-payment when using MediSave to treat chronic disease under the care of a family doctor – as part of an MOH programme.

sections.label: Subsidy tied to physical venue
sections.summary: Tying subsidy to a physical venue can be regressive, so MOH is asked to watch for physical or systemic barriers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Because when subsidy is tied to a physical venue, to a place of bricks and mortar, it can become accidentally regressive because the less well-off – patients and families who are less mobile, they find it harder to get to the place of care, harder to access to the subsidy.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: And it is these families who also find it harder to apply for private medical transport, to foot the bill, to get to the place of care.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: So, I call upon MOH to look closely at this because if the policy intent is to provide subsidy where help is needed, then we have to keep a lookout for physical or systemic barriers.

sections.label: Supporting family doctors for complex patients
sections.summary: A call for MOH to form a Healthier SG workgroup on issues facing long-term patients with serious conditions in the community.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: For patients with advanced neurological conditions, later-stage kidney diseases or dementia – can we find ways to better empower family doctors who have known these patients for years, family doctors who hope for better support from the hospital clusters, to care for patients in the community?

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: I call upon MOH to look at forming a workgroup as part of Healthier SG, to look at the issues faced by long-term patients with serious medical conditions living in the community.

sections.label: Hospital choice under capitation
sections.summary: Asks whether patients will face financial or administrative obstacles choosing a subsidised specialist at a public hospital outside their Healthier SG cluster.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Will there be obstacles to patients choosing which public hospital they can go to, to receive their subsidised specialist care, once capitation kicks in?

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Can MOH confirm that patients will not face uphill hurdles – financial or administrative – if they wish to see a specialist at a different public hospital from the Healthier SG cluster near their home?

sections.label: Time saved on technology
sections.summary: Saving one minute waiting for computers and apps would save 14 million minutes yearly, about 27 years of round-the-clock work.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Imagine if we save one minute on waiting for computers and apps and technology-related time spent — less time spent waiting for technology or grappling with technology.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: That would mean 14 million minutes saved every year – 10,000 workdays, or about 27 years of someone working 24 hours a day.

sections.label: Clinic software, compliance and capitation
sections.summary: Asks if MOH will review clinic software and form-filling, whether small clinics need more staff for Healthier SG compliance, and if capitation reflects differing patient needs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Will MOH look at how the software is designed, how long it takes to fill up a form, whether existing clinic software may become slower and more cumbersome once it connects with the public sector IT network?

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Has MOH assessed whether small clinics will need additional headcounts to address the compliance requirements of joining Healthier SG.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Can I ask the Ministry: will capitation consider that different patients have different needs, some patients having more medical conditions, more illnesses, more complex needs and thereby, more attention and more funding needed to achieve the same healthcare outcome?

sections.label: Diversity and flexible work in healthcare
sections.summary: Calls for deliberate attention to diversity in the healthcare workforce and flexible work arrangements so healthcare workers who are parents or caregivers can keep progressing.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: So, we need to ensure a diversity of backgrounds and journeys in our healthcare workforce, in our medical profession, at every level and in every generation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: There has been progress, but we must continue giving this much deliberate attention, whether it is flexible work arrangements (FWAs) so that healthcare workers who are parents, who are caregivers to an elderly relative who need more flexible arrangements at work, that they can continue training, developing, growing, progressing on their journey.

sections.label: Waiving cash co-payment for CDMP
sections.summary: Under Healthier SG, MOH will waive the requirement for residents to co-pay part of their bills in cash when using MediSave for chronic care management at their family doctor under CDMP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Under Healthier SG, MOH will waive the requirement for residents to co-pay part of their bills in cash when using MediSave for chronic care management at their family doctor under the Chronic Disease Management Programme (CDMP).

sections.label: MediSave limits for chronic care
sections.summary: The speaker calls for annual MediSave withdrawal limits for chronic disease management to be completely lifted, especially for those over 60.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Given the direction of Healthier SG towards waiving cash co-payment requirements for chronic care management, I would like to call for the annual MediSave withdrawal limits for chronic disease management to be completely lifted, especially for those over 60.

sections.label: Drug prices at private clinics
sections.summary: Under Healthier SG, drug prices at participating private family doctor clinics will be made more comparable to polyclinic prices through enhanced subsidies and price limits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Under Healthier SG, drug prices at participating private family doctor clinics will be made "more comparable" to those at polyclinics through a combination of enhanced drug subsidies and drug price limits.

sections.label: Narrowing drug price difference
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Minister to confirm the narrowing of the difference will come only from lowering family doctor patients' drug prices, not raising polyclinic prices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Can the Minister confirm that the "narrowing" of the difference will be brought about only by lowering the price of drugs for patients of family doctors, and not by increasing polyclinic prices to achieve parity?

sections.label: Maternal and child preventive healthcare
sections.summary: The speaker says maternal and child preventive healthcare can potentially reduce long-term healthcare costs but received relatively less attention in the White Paper.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Another area that can potentially reduce healthcare costs in the long term, but was given relatively less attention in the White Paper is maternal and child preventive healthcare.

sections.label: Metrics and targets before Healthier SG
sections.summary: The speaker says both performance metrics and targets should be set before embarking on Healthier SG.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Both performance metrics and targets should be set before embarking on Healthier SG.

sections.label: PQs on preventive health targets
sections.summary: The speaker has filed PQs for the Minister on targets for short- and long-term preventive health metrics, including screening rates, Healthy 365 app use, obesity rate and avoidable emergency department attendance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I have filed PQs to be answered by the Minister tomorrow on the targets for various short- and long-term preventive health metrics.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: These include the target screening rates for chronic diseases, the proportion of residents actively using the Healthy 365 app, the obesity rate and the avoidable emergency department attendance rate.

sections.label: Releasing taxpayer-funded survey results
sections.summary: The Government should release taxpayer-funded survey results to inform the public on future healthcare spending and prompt lifestyle adjustments under Healthier SG.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Given that the survey was funded by taxpayers, the Government should release the survey results, so as to better inform the public on issues regarding future healthcare spending, and prompt them, as is the objective of Healthier SG, to make the necessary adjustments to their lifestyles and preparations to avert preventable chronic illnesses in the future.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: This plan is a strategic move to transform Singapore's healthcare system from one that primarily cares for the sick to one that proactively prevents sickness.

sections.label: Facilitating GP transition to consultative care
sections.summary: The question asks how the Ministry facilitates a busy GP's transition to more consultative, holistic care taking more time.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: How does the Ministry facilitate the transition, for example, of a GP who sees, say 50 to 60 patients a day, a popular one, to morph into one that is more consultative, holistic and takes a lot more time?

sections.label: Regional health system, jobs, technology costs
sections.summary: The question asks what regional health system players would do differently, the resident experience, jobs and skills needed, and IT maintenance costs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: What would the regional health system player each in charge of about 1.5 million residents do differently?

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: With so many partners and touchpoints, what would the typical experience of an enrolled resident to Healthy SG or the system or a "customer" look like in his healthcare journey?

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: For Singaporeans to appreciate the big shift and the need for greater investments – I think the Minister had just announced as $1 billion for a start and I think $400 million for recurring costs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: What are the types of jobs, in detail, what are the skills pre-requisites and number of persons required to realise the vision of Healthier SG?

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: On technology, beyond the one-time grant to assist clinics, if they do convert, to convert to an appropriate IT system, how would the maintenance and upgrade costs be treated?

sections.label: Enrolment rates and aggressive marketing
sections.summary: Resident enrolment or health plan completion rates can easily be ramped up through aggressive marketing without regard for quality or follow up.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Resident enrolment rate or health plan completion rates can easily be ramped up through aggressive marketing, without regard for quality or follow up.

sections.label: Family physician numbers and 2030 target
sections.summary: The question asks whether the 3,500 family physician target by 2030 remains valid and how the increase will be catered for.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: At the end of FY2021, the membership of the College of Family Physicians Singapore registered just over 2,600 doctors providing primary care, of whom there are approximately 1,600 doctors holding a graduate diploma of family medicine qualification.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: MOH previously estimated that in order to implement our plans, 3,500 family physicians are required by 2030 – more or less doubling the number in just seven years.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Could the Minister clarify if these targets remain valid?

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Given the long time needed for doctors to be trained – five years of medical school in Singapore, plus the five years to serve the bond – would the Ministry clarify how it intends for such an increase in numbers to be catered for by 2030?

sections.label: Increasing primary and community care doctors
sections.summary: The White Paper mentions increasing doctors and nurses in primary and community care from one-fifth to at least a quarter by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The White Paper mentions the need to increase the number of doctors and nurses in primary and community care from the current one-fifth to at least a quarter by 2030.

sections.label: Perceptions of family doctors
sections.summary: A study found half of medical students would consider general practice, but perceived fewer career options and encountered derogatory comments about poor clinical competence.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: She mentioned that the initial reaction to hearing that somebody is a family doctor is that they "didn't quite make the grade to become a specialist".

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: These concerns are backed up by a pertinent study done by the Lee Kong Chian School of Medicine under the leadership of Prof Helen Smith, which found that while half of medical students would consider a career in general practice and family medicine (GPFM), the perception was that there were less career advancement options.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Perhaps of more concern was the finding that students reported having encountered derogatory comments about the area, including doctors in GPFM having "poor clinical competence".

sections.label: Primary care clinics and mental health
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether MOH would work with MND and HDB on heartland clinics, and notes mental health is not among the first 12 care protocols.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This is especially important if we are trying to attract more doctors to provide primary care.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Also, would MOH work closely with the Ministry of National Development (MND) and the Housing and Development Board (HDB) in particular, to ensure that our family doctors are able to easily set up clinics in our heartlands and that their practices remain available and accessible to our communities?

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: While the White Paper mentions mental health protocols will be developed, mental health does not appear to be part of the first 12 care protocols being rolled out to family doctors.

sections.label: Life expectancy gender gap
sections.summary: A 2017 MOH report with the Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation found the female-male gap between life expectancy and healthy life expectancy grew from 2.4 to 2.5 years between 1990 and 2017.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: A 2017 MOH report in collaboration with the Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation found that in 1990, the gap between life expectancy and healthy life expectancy was 2.4 years larger for females compared with males and this had increased to 2.5 years by 2017.

sections.label: Pelvic floor conditions in women
sections.summary: Prolapse and stress urinary incontinence are thought to affect at least 15% of women in Singapore, and embarrassment may mean many suffer in silence.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Issues such as prolapse and stress urinary incontinence due to the weakening of pelvic floor muscles, whether brought on by menopause or childbirth, are thought to affect at least 15% of women here in Singapore, yet embarrassment to discuss such matters even to obstetrician-gynaecologists (OBGYNs) probably means that many women suffer needlessly in silence for what is often a treatable condition.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: To sum up, we support Healthier SG and believe that this approach will benefit Singapore in the long run.

sections.label: Patients, staff and chronic disease
sections.summary: The speaker says prevention and care system performance depend on patients and staff, and notes 32% of the population has hypertension and 37% hyperlipidaemia.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: After all, we can talk until we are blue in the face about the twin "P"s of prevention and the performance of our care systems, but these will be nowhere without the two most important "P"s of the system – our patients and the incredible people who make the system run.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Age aside, there is a prevalence of chronic diseases amongst our population – 32% of our population has hypertension and 37% has hyperlipidaemia.

sections.label: Vaping deaths and lung injury
sections.summary: As of 18 February 2020, vaping was linked to 68 deaths and over 2,800 cases of EVALI in the United States.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: As of 18 February 2020, vaping has been linked to 68 deaths and over 2,800 cases of lung injury related to vaping – now more commonly referred to as EVALI, E-cigarette or Vaping product use-Associated Lung Injury, in the United States.

sections.label: Chemicals found in products
sections.summary: Chemicals found included formaldehyde, nicotine levels above a cigarette, and juice containing THC.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Among the chemicals found was formaldehyde, a cancer-causing agent used in the process of embalming, nicotine levels which surpassed a stick of cigarette and juice laced with tetrahydrocannabinol (THC), the main psychoactive compound found in marijuana.

sections.label: Regional health managers role
sections.summary: NHG, NUHS and SingHealth will act as regional health managers for about 1.5 million residents each, working with family doctors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In the White Paper, the National Healthcare Group (NHG), National University Health System (NUHS) and SingHealth (SHS) will step up as regional health managers to look after the health of approximately 1.5 million residents in their respective sectors each and work with family doctors and other partners to reach out to as many residents as possible.

sections.label: Healthier SG rollout timing
sections.summary: Enrolment starts for those aged 60 and above in the second half of 2023, and the question asks when the rest of the population will follow.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: With enrolment starting for those aged 60 and above in the second half of 2023, will Healthier SG be rolled out to the rest of the population and if yes, when do we expect that to happen?

sections.label: Dementia numbers in Singapore
sections.summary: 60,000 people aged 60 and above live with dementia today, projected to reach 90,000 residents by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Today, 60,000 people aged 60 and above live with dementia.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: By 2030, it is projected that 90,000 residents will be living with dementia in Singapore.

sections.label: Dementia care cost
sections.summary: The cost of caring for a dementia patient is above $40,000 per year and continues to rise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The cost of taking care of a dementia patient is above $40,000 per year and continues to rise.

sections.label: Care protocols rollout question
sections.summary: The question asks the Minister to elaborate on the 12 care protocols and their expected full rollout time beyond Healthier SG's first year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Beyond the mentioned first three chronic illnesses, may I ask the Minister to elaborate more on the 12 care protocols and the time it is expected to take for the care protocols to be fully rolled out beyond the first year of Healthier SG?

sections.label: Family physician mental health role
sections.summary: Asks whether the task force will consider enhancing the family physician's role in managing residents' mental health.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Will the task force consider how the family physician's role in managing the mental health of their residents can be enhanced?

sections.label: Regular family doctor continuity
sections.summary: Asks how MOH will harmonise GP changes when employees or employers change with Healthier SG's aim of one regular family doctor.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: When employees change employment or if their employers change their insurers, the GPs or clinics may also change.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: I would like to ask how does MOH intend to harmonise this situation with its proposed programme under Healthier SG to have more people stick to one regular family doctor?

sections.label: Consultation and prescription costs
sections.summary: Asks how MOH will ensure consultation and prescription costs with the family physician do not discourage switching to Healthier SG.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Besides MOH's plans to make available more prescribed drugs under CHAS subsidy in GP clinics, how will MOH ensure that the cost of consultations and prescriptions with the family physician will not discourage Singaporeans from switching to Healthier SG?

sections.label: Extending Healthier SG to dental
sections.summary: Asks whether MOH will in future extend Healthier SG to cover dental and oral healthcare.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: In my view, a similarly structured programme akin to Healthier SG may also help to promote better dental and oral health.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: I would, therefore, like to know whether in the future, if MOH will also look at extending Healthier SG to the coverage of dental and oral healthcare.

sections.label: MediSave and CHAS subsidies
sections.summary: A resident wishes the Government would consider making MediSave available and increasing CHAS subsidies for some treatments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: While there are subsidies available for limited categories of CHAS and other card holders, my resident wishes that the Government can consider making MediSave available for at least some of the treatments and/or consider increasing the extent of CHAS subsidies currently available for these treatments, for example, for orange CHAS card holders and even beyond.

sections.label: Family doctor patient loading
sections.summary: Asks MOH's expectation on the effect of additional work or patient loading from Healthier SG if patient numbers do not reduce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: While they will be paid a fee per enrolled resident, if the patient numbers do not reduce for any family doctor, what is the expectation of MOH on the effect of the additional work or additional patient loading brought about by Healthier SG?

sections.label: Eldercare centres expansion plan
sections.summary: The White Paper plans to increase existing eldercare centres from 119 to 220 by 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: The White Paper also plans to increase the number of existing eldercare centres from 119 to 220 by 2025.

sections.label: Burden and GST increase
sections.summary: It is a growing financial and emotional burden on families and was cited as the reason for raising GST despite the political cost.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: It is a growing financial and emotional burden on our families.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: It has already been cited as the reason why we have to do the unpopular choice and raise GST, despite the political cost.

sections.label: Health adjusted life expectancy
sections.summary: MOH has tried measuring health adjusted life expectancy, which has been increasing year-on-year, and at 73.9% in 2019 is the highest in the world.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: And she may want to know for the specific datapoint on health adjusted life expectancy (HALE), MOH has actually tried doing that and it has been increasing year-on-year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: And based on the global finding, our HALE at 73.9% in 2019 is the highest in the world.

sections.label: Spending on acute care
sections.summary: Too much has been spent on acute care and too little on prevention.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Too much has been spent on acute care, too little on prevention.

sections.label: Health outcomes as Healthier SG pillar
sections.summary: The speaker calls on MOH to consider including a drive to accelerate identification, measurement and transparency of health outcomes as another pillar of Healthier SG.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I repeat, not something we can leave to the clusters.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: So, I call on MOH to consider including, as another pillar of Healthier SG, a drive to accelerate the identification, measurement and transparency of health outcomes.

sections.label: Complications and cost reductions
sections.summary: In the first two years, complications decreased by 18%, re-operations by 23%, and revisions by 19%, with cost per patient declining 14% in provider resources and 20% in money paid out by the Council.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In the first two years, complications decreased by 18%, re-operations by 23%, and revisions by 19%, cost per patient declined 14% in terms of resources used by providers and 20% in terms of money paid out by the Council.

sections.label: GP visit after discharge
sections.summary: Lumos data suggests a GP visit within one week of discharge of an unplanned re-admission can substantially reduce risk of unplanned hospitalisation five to 12 weeks after discharge.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Lumos data also suggests a GP visit within one week of discharge of an unplanned re-admission can substantially reduce the risk of an unplanned hospitalisation in the five to 12 weeks following discharge.

sections.label: Payment reforms for quality
sections.summary: Healthcare systems worldwide are implementing payment reforms with mixed results, paying for quality and value rather than volume.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This is why healthcare systems around the world are implementing payment reforms, with mixed results.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: There are different forms – pay for performance, bundled payments, capitation and they can be used in combination, but the fundamental logic is the same – pay for quality and value rather than volume.

sections.label: CMS Medicare Advantage example
sections.summary: CMS Medicare Advantage in the US pays private insurers a fixed risk-adjusted payment for a patient's total cost of care.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: One successful example is CMS Medicare Advantage in the US, where Medicare pays private insurers a fixed risk-adjusted payment for the total cost of care for a patient.

sections.label: Capitation prerequisites and Healthier SG
sections.summary: Capitation needs defined patient groups, risk adjustment and quality thresholds, and the MP asks how Healthier SG's capitation payments will be risk adjusted.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: These successful models point to a few prerequisites for capitation to be truly value-based.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: It needs to be organised around defined patient groups and population segments, adjusted for risk, and linked to quality thresholds or improvement in health outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Otherwise, capitation could create incentives for "cherry-picking" of healthier patients or for limiting access to required care or what we call "rationing" behaviour.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: To that end, can the Minister clarify the capitation model envisioned under Healthier SG, including how will the payments be risk adjusted based on patient profiles in the cluster?

sections.label: Healthier SG transformation requirements
sections.summary: Healthier SG is a fundamental and comprehensive transformation requiring institutional commitment, investment, and new organisational and people capabilities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Healthier SG is a fundamental and comprehensive transformation that will require institutional commitment to work things out, considerable investment and new organisational and people capabilities and ways of working.

sections.label: Concerns about premature KPI targets
sections.summary: The speaker says setting targets too early without a good base can create perverse target-setting, and favours measuring and identifying the right KPIs first.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: So, which are the KPIs is she not concerned that the hospitals will game?

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
sentences.text: I think I am just making a general point that we have seen in multiple studies, that sometimes target-setting too early when you do not actually have a good base behind it can create a lot of perverse target-setting.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
sentences.text: I am not saying that hospitals will do it, not saying that doctors will do it, but I do not think we need to take that risk and instead focus on the measurement, identifying the right ones in the first place, measuring, and then also making sure that we keep doing better and better in those KPIs.

sections.label: KPIs and transformation targets
sections.summary: The speaker says targets may be set for some KPIs and that the KPIs on the page should be scrutinised first.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
sentences.text: Some KPIs, maybe you can set the target.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
sentences.text: I believe we need to walk before we run.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
sentences.text: This is a very major transformation and like I said, we should scrutinise the KPIs on the page first to make sure that those are the right ones that we want to measure.

sections.label: Paper transforms health care system
sections.summary: The speaker says the paper will transform the health care system into one that is preventive.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: At this juncture, I think I would like to join them as well.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This paper itself will transform our health care system into one that is preventive.

sections.label: White Paper family doctor ratio
sections.summary: The current White Paper dictates one family doctor to one resident.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The current White Paper now dictates that it should be one family doctor to one resident.

sections.label: Medical records and IT
sections.summary: The speaker says good medical records make a big difference and that the key thing now is IT.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: When you have good medical records, then it makes a big difference.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: So, I think the key thing now is your IT.

sections.label: GP referrals across clusters
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Minister to clarify whether GPs in one health cluster can refer patients to specialists in other clusters.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Can the Minister also help clarify whether GPs in a particular health cluster can refer patients to specialists in other clusters, especially for existing patients who have been seeing a doctor at a particular hospital for a long time?

sections.label: Annual service fee for residents
sections.summary: MOH announced an annual service fee per enrolled resident, varying by risk profile, scope of care and progress made.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: MOH has announced that there will be an annual service fee for each enrolled resident, which will vary according to the risk profile, scope of care as well as progress made.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The fees are based on the patient's progress rather than service, which I think could be challenging to measure objectively.

sections.label: Drug pricing and GPs
sections.summary: Drug pricing comparable to polyclinics must be handled carefully as GPs earn from selling proprietary drugs, and uneven rollout may lead residents to prefer polyclinics.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In terms of drug pricing – drug pricing to be made comparable to polyclinics needs to be handled carefully as GPs do earn from the sale of proprietary drugs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The uneven rollout of drug pricing by January 2024 may lead to residents preferring to be seen in polyclinics instead of GPs.

sections.label: GP incentive and workload
sections.summary: The incentive for GPs may not be worth the extra time and effort because in July 2023 the solo GP and clinical assistant must do enormous work.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The incentive for GPs may not be worth the extra time and effort because, in July 2023 – that is, next year – the solo GP and his clinical assistant must do an enormous amount of work.

sections.label: Health cluster KPIs and GP groups
sections.summary: The Ministry is asked for specific health cluster KPIs and how they will be tracked, and small GP groups and independent GPs may be disadvantaged.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Can the Ministry share what are the specific KPIs for the health clusters and how will these KPIs be tracked?

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I would also like to raise the concern that small GP groups as well as independent GPs may find themselves at a disadvantage, compared to the big groups which have clinics spanning all three clusters, because their market will be very limited.

sections.label: MOH monitoring GP workload
sections.summary: MOH is asked how it will monitor the situation to ensure GPs are well-equipped to deal with increasing workload.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: How will MOH monitor the situation to ensure that GPs are well-equipped to deal with increasing workload?

sections.label: IT, manpower, respect
sections.summary: Three things are raised: IT support, manpower, and respect for healthcare workers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Three things: one, IT support; two, manpower; and three, the elephant in the room, respect for healthcare workers.

sections.label: Replacing experienced ICU nurse
sections.summary: It is asked whether losing one nurse with 10 years of experience and ICU training can be replaced by five new nurses.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Losing one nurse with 10 years of experience and intensive care unit (ICU) training, can she be replaced by five new nurses?

sections.label: PR status for healthcare workers
sections.summary: Asks whether PR status could be offered to healthcare workers after one to two years and to immediate family after five years.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Would it be possible to consider offering permanent resident (PR) status for the healthcare worker after one to two years of working here and maybe even extending PR status to the immediate family after a longer period of work, let us say, five years?

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Specialists have raised concerns about the capitation model in particular, will there be funding for complex cases, such as transplants or if a routine case runs into complications?

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In the long run, we worry that the quality of care will be affected adversely as well as our standing as a leading medical health hub.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: After the hurrah of healthcare heroes during COVID-19, we now struggle with a backload of "business as usual" cases, long waiting times and general unhappiness.

sections.label: Health education for patients
sections.summary: Says good basic health education and understanding of how the body works is essential to keeping oneself healthy.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I wonder, do people argue with lawyers or bankers this much in legal or financial matters?

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I always believe that education is key: good basic health education and understanding of how our body system works, how the body gets ill – is essential towards keeping oneself healthy.

sections.label: Healthier SG community care shift
sections.summary: Looks forward to Healthier SG shifting care to community-based care and embodying prevention is better than cure.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In the launch of Healthier SG, I look forward to the shift of care to a community-based care and truly embody "prevention is better than cure".

sections.label: Clawback for GP non-performance
sections.summary: Asks whether there will be provisions for clawback of fees or termination for non-performance, given capitation payments.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Since we are paying the GPs and regional health managers on a capita basis, and learning from the SportsHub experience, will there be provisions for clawback of fees paid or termination for non-performance?

sections.label: Service fees for foreigners
sections.summary: Asks whether service fees paid to GPs and healthcare clusters will differ between foreigners and locals.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: For the service fees that the Government will be paying to GPs and healthcare clusters, will there be any difference between foreigners and locals?

sections.label: Healthcare professional numbers projection
sections.summary: Asks for the number of doctors, nurses and other healthcare professionals now and projected in the next decade.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: What are the number of doctors, nurses, and other healthcare professionals now and projected in the next decade?

sections.label: MediSave for outpatient treatment
sections.summary: A question asks whether MOH will consider allowing MediSave to be used for all outpatient treatment, in line with the White Paper.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In line with the efforts outlined in the White Paper to move our healthcare more towards preventive and primary healthcare, will MOH consider allowing MediSave to be used for all outpatient treatment?

sections.label: GPs for elderly residents
sections.summary: A question asks whether there will be enough GPs and community partners to support elderly residents in Kolam Ayer and Jalan Besar GRC.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: For example, as a whole, in my constituency at Kolam Ayer and Jalan Besar GRC, there are higher proportions of elderly residents and notably, there may be fewer GP clinics in the vicinity too.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Therefore, concerning resources, both in terms of quantity and quality, will there be enough GPs and community partners that can support our elderly?

sections.label: Enrolling caregivers with elderly
sections.summary: A question asks whether caregivers can be enrolled with the elderly in their charge.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Would it be possible to allow the caregivers to be enrolled with the elderly in their charge?

sections.label: Mental health in Healthier SG
sections.summary: A question asks how the Ministry plans to address these concerns and how mental health fits in the Healthier SG initiative.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: How, then, does the Ministry plan to address these concerns?

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Thus, I would like to ask the Ministry: how does mental health fit in the Healthier SG initiative?

sections.label: GPs and mental health screening
sections.summary: A statement says GPs would increase accessibility nodes and expresses hope that health screening can include mental health aspects.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: GPs now would naturally increase the nodes for accessibility, and I hope health screening can also include aspects of mental health.

sections.label: BMI and body fat goals
sections.summary: A speaker describes shifting BMI from overweight and lowering body fat from 25% to 20%, shedding about 10 kilogrammes, and meeting the objectives.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: To shift my BMI category from overweight to something more acceptable and lowering my body fat percentage from 25% to 20%.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: This means shedding about 10 kilogrammes off my deceivingly "okay-looking" frame.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I am glad to share that I have met the objectives, but there are a few lessons learnt.

sections.label: Support for the Motion
sections.summary: The speaker supports the Motion despite concerns shared earlier.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding my concerns shared earlier, I support the Motion.

sections.label: Singapore healthcare rankings
sections.summary: Legatum Institute ranked Singapore second for Health in its 2021 index, and a WHO study ranked Singapore sixth globally.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Legatum Institute ranked Singapore number two in the world for the Health Pillar in their Legatum Prosperity Index (LPI) 2021.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The WHO's global study assesses healthcare systems around the world and Singapore was ranked sixth in the world, and the highest rank for countries outside of Europe.

sections.label: Diabetic population budget investment
sections.summary: Investing an additional 4% of the budget in the diabetic population decreased hospital admissions by 22% and other avoidable visits by 21%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For their diabetic population, they invested additional 4% of their budget in this group and achieved a decrease in hospital admits by 22% and a decrease of 21% for other avoidable visits and admissions, resulting in overall improvement in value of care and reducing overall costs over time.

sections.label: Enrolment with GP or doctor
sections.summary: The speaker asks MOH to clarify whether intended enrolment is with a GP practice or clinic or with a named doctor.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Can MOH clarify if the intended enrolment is with a GP practice/clinic or is it with a named doctor?

sections.label: Phased approach and enrolment groups
sections.summary: The speaker calls the phased approach pragmatic and hopes MOH considers enrolling IHL and NS groups and lowering the starting age to 40.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Phased approach is the pragmatic way to implement.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I am above 60, and so am in the category – but after listening to hon Members speak about it, I do hope that MOH can consider enrolling the students in Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs) and the National Service (NS) groups as well as reduce the starting age to 40, because usually it is the 40-something who will bring the 70-something to the doctor.

sections.label: Onboarding digitally naive citizens
sections.summary: The speaker asks how MOH will onboard digitally naive citizens likely from lower-income households.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: How will MOH onboard this segment of citizens who are digitally naive and who are likely to be from the lower-income households?

sections.label: Healthier SG for PRs, pass holders
sections.summary: Asks how Healthier SG will apply to permanent residents, employment pass holders and work permit holders.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Lastly, considering that we do have a sizeable number of people in our community who are permenant residents (PRs) and employment pass holders or work permit holders, how will Healthier SG apply to them?

sections.label: Value-based care model opportunity
sections.summary: Says Singapore can create an innovative value-based care model, and notes the debate on the Healthier SG White Paper.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: At the same time, there is opportunity for Singapore to create an innovative model of value-based care based on strong population health expertise with a robust digital health platform, an extensive telehealth network and a compassionate and engaged community.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Today, we are debating a new health and healthcare strategy for Singapore, laid out in the White Paper on Healthier SG.

sections.label: Healthier SG White Paper landmark strategy
sections.summary: Calls the White Paper a landmark providing a strategy reboot for a different population and larger healthcare budget.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Thirty years on, we have this White Paper on Healthier SG.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: And I believe it will be no less of a landmark paper, providing an additional strategy – a strategy reboot – for a vastly different population with very different needs and against the backdrop of a Government healthcare budget that has increased many times in the last 10 years.

sections.label: Healthy 365 app digital front door
sections.summary: States the Healthy 365 app will be the digital front door for enrolling with a family doctor and tracking behaviour.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: The Healthy 365 app will be the "digital front door" for citizens to enrol with a family doctor and Healthy 365 will also be the "digital front door" for capturing individual behaviour, for tracking progress and for generating healthpoints in exchange for rewards.

sections.label: Avoid digital gate in Healthier SG
sections.summary: Warns a digital front door in Healthier SG could become a digital gate for some, which must be avoided.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: A "digital front door" in Healthier SG can well become a "digital gate" for some and we have to avoid that.

sections.label: Healthier SG chronic disease focus
sections.summary: States Healthier SG focuses on chronic diseases, preventing onset and managing diseases well if inevitable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: The focus of Healthier SG is chronic diseases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Prevent chronic disease onset in the first instance and if disease is inevitable, manage these diseases well.

sections.label: Centralising clinical manpower deployment
sections.summary: The speaker suggests centralising clinical manpower recruitment, posting and deployment across the three healthcare clusters at Ministry level.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: On a related note, may I suggest even more boldly, that clinical manpower recruitment, posting and deployment in general across our three healthcare clusters, should be centralised at the Ministry level going forward?

sections.label: Capitation funding through healthcare clusters
sections.summary: The speaker proposes capitation funding to GPs flow through healthcare clusters rather than MOH, aspiring to a UK-style model of direct hospital admission.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: My fourth broad point: on healthcare financing, our reforms can go further to truly drive integration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Ideally, capitation funding to GPs should flow through the healthcare clusters rather than from MOH, as is currently proposed in the White Paper.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Capitation funding to GPs through the clusters will drive fuller integrations between GPs and the clusters as regional health managers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: We should aspire to – as many Members have mentioned – the UK model for example, where GPs can eventually refer patients for direct admission to a hospital within a healthcare cluster, without the need to go through an Emergency Department, for clinically appropriate cases.

sections.label: HPB exercise groups attendance concerns
sections.summary: Residents worry that some HPB exercise groups could be cut or consolidated for not maintaining a certain attendance rate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: For example, exercise groups by HPB had emerged with a vengeance since we opened up and residents have really welcomed this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: But recently, there has been concerns amongst residents that some of the exercise groups by HPB could be cut or consolidated away because they are not hitting and maintaining a certain attendance rate.

sections.label: Community exercise groups and health activities
sections.summary: The speaker says every local community needs community exercise groups and health promoting activities, even if this means some redundancy or unused capacity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: We need each and every local community to be abuzz and completely teeming with community exercise groups and health promoting activities catering to the entire range of needs and lifestyles within the community.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: This will really bring Healthier SG alive in the community and send a strong signal to residents that we want them on board, even if this may mean some redundancy or unused capacity at the margins.

sections.label: Taxing unhealthy food and Healthier SG
sections.summary: The speaker asks Ms Hazel Poa whether taxing unhealthy food would cohere with Healthier SG, and describes Healthier SG as a moonshot.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
sentences.text: Member Ms Hazel Poa suggested taxing unhealthy food to subsidise healthy food.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
sentences.text: And I would just like to ask her for clarifications about her specific ideas for taxing unhealthy food and in the larger spirit of Healthier SG, having heard the essence of the strategy, whether she feels that, an intervention like taxing unhealthy food would cohere with the overall spirit of the strategy and is still a good idea.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
sentences.text: — one family doctor was quoted as describing Healthier SG as "our great leap forward for primary care and preventive care for chronic conditions." But a "great leap forward" may not end up in success.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
sentences.text: So, I prefer to see Healthier SG as a "moonshot" for SG Healthcare.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
sentences.text: And when JF Kennedy resolved to send a man to the Moon, he said, "We choose to go to the Moon in this decade and do the other things, not because they are easy, but because they are hard." Indeed, Healthier SG entails hard work ahead for us in this decade, very hard work.

sections.label: Union cases on workplace grievances
sections.summary: Of the many cases unions handle, only about 10% are on workplace grievances.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Of the many cases that unions handle, only about 10% are on workplace grievances.

sections.label: Health screening replaces medical leave incentive
sections.summary: Members were offered $50 to skip medical leave, now replaced by an annual health screening worth close to $150.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Initially, our members were offered $50 if they chose not to take any medical leave for the year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We have replaced that with an annual health screening worth close to $150.

sections.label: Member health screening subsidy
sections.summary: Subsidy ranges from $50 to $100 per member, and over 2,200 members received more than $150,000 total as of today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This subsidy ranges from $50 to $100 per member, depending on the cost of additional tests that our members would like to take.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We are pleased to share that we have supported more than 2,200 members with a total subsidy of more than $150,000 as of today and we intend to reach out to more members.

sections.label: MediSave for additional medical checks
sections.summary: The question asks whether the Ministry can allow individuals to use MediSave for additional medical checks for their own well-being.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Can the Ministry also allow an individual to use their MediSave for additional medical checks that they want to do for their own well-being?

sections.label: Good health and Healthier SG mission
sections.summary: The speaker says good health is real wealth and urges working together to eat healthier and adopt a healthy lifestyle for Healthier SG.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: (In English): Madam, many of us would acknowledge that good health is the real wealth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is one where we can enjoy benefits of our hard work, instead of sacrificing our savings and wealth to pay for our medical costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Let us work together to eat healthier food and adopt a healthy lifestyle so that we can all achieve our mission towards a Healthier SG.

sections.label: Prioritising those above 55
sections.summary: Prioritising those above 55 is crucial because about one in four Singaporeans will be 65 or older in 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Prioritising those above 55 is crucial, given that about one in four Singaporeans will be 65 years old and older in 2030.

sections.label: National enrollment programme changes
sections.summary: Singaporeans will be allowed up to four changes in the initial enrollment period, but its length was unclear.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: With regard to the national enrollment programme, it was stated that Singaporeans will be allowed up to four changes in the initial enrollment period but it was unclear how long the enrollment period would be.

sections.label: GP medication subsidy and capitation
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Government would consider this group of GPs for medication subsidy and capitation funding.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Would the Government consider this group of GPs in terms of medication subsidy and capitation funding?

sections.label: Employers and family doctor enrolment
sections.summary: The passage states a clarification question on how the Ministry intends to work with employers to help employees enrol in family doctor national enrolment programmes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: One question for clarification will be how the Ministry intends to work with employers in assisting their employees to enrol in family doctor national enrolment programmes.

sections.label: Seeing panel doctors for episodic care
sections.summary: The passage states that seeing panel doctors for episodic care despite national programme enrolment derails the core idea of keeping to one primary care doctor.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: While Singaporeans can choose to see the panel doctors for episodic care despite enrolling in the national programme, it derails from the core idea of keeping to one primary care doctor, limiting the true benefit of having a dedicated family doctor.

sections.label: Insurers integrating MediSave-related policies
sections.summary: The passage states MOH and MAS should encourage the Life Insurance Association to find sustainable ways to integrate this into MediSave-related policies, with healthier plans paying less when premiums rise with age.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: MOH and the monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) should encourage the Life Insurance Association to find sustainable ways to integrate this to an individual's MediSave-related policies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: For example, those with committed healthier plans should not be paying as much when premiums increase with age.

sections.label: Engaging society for preventive care
sections.summary: The passage states that shifting to preventive care requires engaging employers and insurers to recalibrate cost calculations and incentives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: As we take the bold step to shift the model to one of preventive care, we will need to engage various aspects of society, including employers and insurers, to recalibrate various cost calculations and incentives.

sections.label: Subsidised vaccinations, screenings and Screen for Life
sections.summary: The passage asks whether fully subsidised nationally recommended vaccinations and screenings are under Screen for Life or added under Healthier SG, and asks the current Screen for Life participation rate for Singaporeans above 50.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The White Paper outlined MOH's plan to fully subsidise nationally recommended vaccinations and screenings as well as an onboarding health consultation with their chosen family doctors upon enrolment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Are they those that are under the existing Screen for Life programme or will there be more added under Healthier SG?

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: What is the participation rate for Screen for Life for Singaporeans above 50 years old currently?

sections.label: Enrolment start for older residents
sections.summary: Enrolment will start next June, beginning with residents aged 60 and above first.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Lastly, I understand that enrolment will start next June, beginning with our older residents aged 60 and above first.

sections.label: Adoption rates of two apps
sections.summary: The speaker asks MOH for adoption rates of two apps by seniors above 60 and how MOH will help them use the apps.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Thus, I would like to clarify with MOH on the current adoption rates for these two apps by the senior population above 60 years old.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: And if the take-up rates have been low, similar to my fellow hon Member, Ms Denise Phua, I would like to ask how MOH intends to help our seniors utilise these two apps after they have enrolled with their family doctors under Healthier SG.

sections.label: Promoting HealthHub and Healthy365 apps
sections.summary: The speaker hopes MOH will work with IMDA to promote HealthHub and Healthy365 apps through the Senior Go-Digital Scheme and teach seniors their functions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This will also help to strengthen the Healthier SG ecosystem.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I also hope that MOH will work with IMDA to promote HealthHub and Healthy365 apps through the IMDA's Senior Go-Digital Scheme and teach the seniors how to use these two apps and introduce their main functions.

sections.label: Reducing administrative work for professionals
sections.summary: The speaker suggests reducing claims administrative work, including doing away with MCs for mild acute illnesses, and investing in subsidised telehealth.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: To the Minister for Health Mr Ong Ye Kung, I agree that administrative work that is required for claims is very necessary, but I think we should study some of the areas in which we can maybe reduce for the professionals.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This can include doing away with the need for issuing medical certificates (MCs) for mild acute illnesses, like coughs and colds, which my fellow hon Member Ms Mariam Jaafar has raised earlier in the Parliamentary speech she made.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: While this will require the support of the Ministry of Defense (MINDEF), the Ministry of Education (MOE) and MOM, countries like the United Kingdom that have practised doing away with MCs for absence from school and work due to common colds and coughs have not seen students or employees abusing such a move.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Also, more use of telehealth, that can augment and take away some of the family doctors' repetitive tasks, should continue to be invested in and subsidised by MOH.

sections.label: Funding model based on health outcomes
sections.summary: The speaker raises concern about the funding model partly based on health outcomes, with service fee payments partially based on preventive care or chronic disease management progress.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: One of my concerns is regarding the funding model that will be partly based on health outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The White Paper states that service fee payments for family doctors will be partially based on "the progress made in terms of preventive care or chronic diseases management".

sections.label: One-off IT support grant
sections.summary: The White Paper states that in the initial phase, the Ministry will provide a one-off IT support grant.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The White Paper states that in the initial phase, the Ministry will provide a one-off IT support grant.

sections.label: Drug subsidy cost checks
sections.summary: The Ministry is asked how it will keep costs in check, while the narrowing of drug subsidy differences is applauded.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: How would the Ministry ensure that costs will be kept in check?

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I applaud the decision to narrow the difference in drug subsidies across polyclinics and private clinics through a combination of enhanced drug subsidies and drug price limits.

sections.label: Proposed SG healthy fund
sections.summary: A hope is expressed that the Ministry considers a SG healthy fund with a steering committee to support healthy living projects.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Similar to the concept of SG Eco Fund, I hope that the Ministry can consider setting up a SG healthy fund to support projects that champion healthy living and involve the community.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: A steering committee can be set up comprising representatives from the 3P sectors, retired grassroots advisors, sports athletes as well as healthy lifestyle experts to manage this fund and monitor the progress of such projects.

sections.label: Funding GP health talks
sections.summary: Funding support is suggested for GPs to hold community health awareness talks and follow-ups like complimentary screening and consultation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: As such, to foster more of such GP-patient relationships, with trust being built up and utilised to deliver the message from Healthier SG, one suggestion would be to consider providing funding support for GPs to conduct health awareness talks for the community, educating our residents about the benefits of preserving one's health with good habits.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Additional funding support can also be considered to encourage organising the follow-ups on the health awareness talks, such as one-time complimentary health screening and consultation sessions for attendees at their neighbourhood GP.

sections.label: PCF Sparkletots card distribution
sections.summary: Nine PCF Sparkletots centres in Woodgrove will procure additional card sets and distribute them to K2 students in 2023.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: For a start, the nine PCF Sparkletots centres across Woodgrove will be procuring additional sets of these playing cards and distributing them to all of our K2 students in 2023.

sections.label: Incentivising healthier food options
sections.summary: Help can come from influencing dietary habits, including calling on fast food chains, film theatres and supermarkets to incentivise healthier options.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Although we can achieve much by encouraging residents to pay more attention to their health, more help can be provided by influencing their dietary habits, such as reducing the cost of healthier food items, which have a reputation for being more expensive than the standard options.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Not just among the ordinary residents, but businesses that serve the community as a whole.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: This includes calling on fast food chains, film theatres and supermarkets, to just to name a few, to explore ways to incentivise offering of healthier options.

sections.label: Combining Western and TCM medicine
