sections.summary: Seniors tend to prefer TCM, and combining Western and TCM medicine in treatment and awareness should be looked into.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Generally, seniors tend to prefer opting for TCM to improve their vitality and address underlying root causes of health concerns in a holistic manner.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I believe, we should look into combining Western and TCM medicine in terms of treatment as well as increasing awareness.

sections.label: Public health intervention return on investment
sections.summary: From 52 studies of healthcare systems in high-income countries, the median return on investment of public health interventions was 14 to one.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: From 52 studies of healthcare systems in high-income countries, it was found that the return on investment (ROI) of public health interventions was at the median of 14 to one, that, is, for every one dollar invested in public health, $14 will be subsequently returned to the wider health and social care economy.

sections.label: Healthier SG White Paper indicators
sections.summary: The White Paper lists 22 indicators to assess Healthier SG, including reducing avoidable Emergency Department attendance and elderly fall injury admissions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: On this front, I note that in the White Paper, the Ministry has listed 22 indicators to assess Healthier SG by, including indicators of easing the load on acute facilities, such as reducing the avoidable Emergency Department attendance rate and reducing the admissions of the elderly for fall injuries.

sections.label: Capitation funding objective
sections.summary: The Ministry's stated objective for capitation funding is to create an inherent incentive for providers to focus on preventive care and right siting.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Ministry's stated objective for adopting capitation funding is to, and I quote, "Create an inherent incentive for healthcare providers to focus on preventive care and right siting of patients." Put another way, healthcare providers who keep patients healthy and do not over service their patients will benefit under a system of capitation funding.

sections.label: Overseas capitation funding evidence
sections.summary: Overseas studies show capitation funding models tended to result in patients receiving less treatment compared with fee-for-service models.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I am not saying this will happen for Healthier SG but we should be alive to the risk.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: There is evidence from several studies overseas that capitation funding models tended to result in patients receiving less treatment, that is, they went to the doctor less frequently and their treatments tended to cost less than compared with the FFS models.

sections.label: Capitation funding formula tiering
sections.summary: The White Paper states the capitation funding formula will be tiered by health risk profile, scope of care and preventive care progress.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Coming back to Healthier SG, I am pleased to note that the White Paper states that the capitation funding formula "will be tiered based on the health risk profile of each enrolled resident, scope of required care and the progress made in terms of preventive care for chronic disease management." Could the Ministry clarify what level of granularity will be used to tier the funding, for instance, will the funding be tiered based on the disease diagnosis and the stage of the disease progression?

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Yesterday, the Minister also touched on the overall finance and budget implications of Healthier SG.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: He said that the set-up cost over three to four years would be about $1 billion, while there would be recurrent cost of about $400 million a year, including the annual servicing fee for patients.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Does this mean that the Ministry has already worked out the detailed capitation sums for each health risk profile, and when will this information be published?

sections.label: Risks of capitation funding
sections.summary: Based on studies overseas, there may be risks associated with capitation funding.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: At the same time, based on studies overseas, there may be risks associated with capitation funding.

sections.label: CHAS scheme GP clinics
sections.summary: The Government launched the CHAS scheme, letting residents visit their own GP clinics at polyclinic fees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The Government then launched the CHAS scheme, allowing residents to visit their own GP clinics at the price of polyclinic fees.

sections.label: Balance of need and demand
sections.summary: The Member asks the Ministry how the balance between need and demand for certain medications will be maintained.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In addition, I would like to ask the Ministry how will the balance be maintained between need and demand for certain medications.

sections.label: Uncooperative patients and clinics
sections.summary: The Member asks what would happen to doctors or clinics with uncooperative patients who have problems adhering to healthcare plans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Next, may I ask what would happen to the doctors or clinics in the case of uncooperative patients with problems adhering to their healthcare plans?

sections.label: Over-enrolment at clinics
sections.summary: The Member asks how it will be resolved if enrolment for particular clinics is always too many for doctors to cope.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: If the enrolment for particular clinics is always too many for the doctors to cope, how will this be resolved?

sections.label: Excuse sheets and health plans
sections.summary: The Member asks whether all employers will recognise such excuse sheets as during COVID-19, and describes doctors advising preventive measures and referrals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Will all employers recognise such "excuse sheet", the same as during COVID-19, when employers must recognise ART-positive results as proof?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: For such residents, the doctor will advise them on appropriate preventive measures as part of their health plans, such as health screenings and vaccinations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The doctor may also make referrals to community programmes.

sections.label: Healthcare financing three elements
sections.summary: Singapore's healthcare financing is described as resting on MediSave, MediShield Life and MediFund, which with subsidies finance only a little more than 8% of national healthcare expenditure.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Singapore's healthcare financing is often described as resting on three key elements, MediSave, MediShield Life and MediFund, which, together with subsidies, characterise the idiosyncratic Singaporean model.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: But it is also worth noting that these three vaunted pillars of the system finance only a little more than 8% of total national healthcare expenditure.

sections.label: Out-of-pocket spending doubled
sections.summary: Dollar spending on out-of-pocket expenditures almost doubled from $448 in 2000 to $821 in 2018, even after accounting for inflation.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Dollar spending on out-of-pocket expenditures, even after accounting for inflation, has almost doubled over the past two decades from $448 in 2000 to $821 in 2018.

sections.label: Monthly family health spending
sections.summary: Singaporean families spend an average of $323 monthly, or 5.5% of incomes, on health expenses, up from 4.9% a decade ago.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Every month, Singaporean families spend an average of $323, or 5.5% of their incomes, on health expenses, an increase from 4.9% just a decade ago.

sections.label: Healthcare burden by income quintile
sections.summary: The highest income quintile devotes 4.8% to healthcare, while the lowest quintile's burden is 7.8%, over one-and-a-half times greater.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: While the highest quintile of income earners devotes 4.8% to healthcare expenditures, the burden on the lowest is more than one-and-a-half times greater at 7.8%.

sections.label: Price guidelines and fee benchmarks
sections.summary: Prohibiting price guidelines may raise costs through differentiation, so regulating a price schedule via the MOH fee benchmark is suggested instead.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Prohibitions on price guidelines, in this case, may merely induce market participants to pursue greater differentiation through the inclusion of bells and whistles, which could paradoxically elevate their costs and in turn, prices charged.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Hence, the decision by the Competition Commission of Singapore to prohibit price guidelines issued by Singapore Medical Association (SMA) may make sense insofar as we are looking at a market comprised of a small number of providers.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: But this hardly describes, in general, the physician market.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It would seem to me that regulating the price schedule, per se, with the inclusion of a wide range of representatives, including academics and MOH-appointed doctors and medical professionals, as has been implemented by the MOH fee benchmark, would be better than allowing prices to be completely unmoored from any guidance whatsoever.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: One approach is to require all physicians post the multiplier of their charges, relative to the benchmark's median.

sections.label: Removing healthcare provider panels
sections.summary: Removing healthcare provider panels could pressure non-panel doctors to rein in charges once prices are no longer the main criteria for panel membership.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The upshot of such a move, as the Life Insurance Association (LIA) itself has allowed, is the possibility of removing healthcare provider panels.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: With prices no longer the main criteria for panel membership, non-panel doctors will face more pressures to rein in their charges.

sections.label: Carrying over pre-existing conditions
sections.summary: Excluding pre-existing conditions consigns patients to their current insurer, so the Government could mandate carrying over pre-existing conditions.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: For instance, allowing the exclusion of pre-existing conditions effectively consigns most patients to their current insurer, once such conditions are developed and identified.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: But if we value the inherent natural justice in taking care of the chronically ill and believe that competition among insurance would work to contain the inevitable increases in premiums, then the Government can resolve the coordination problem by mandating the carrying over of pre-existing conditions, because any insurer would never want to be the first mover.

sections.label: $2 billion facility cost
sections.summary: The $2 billion facility's cost was compounded by the record-setting $1.25 billion land sale it sits on.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The cost of the $2 billion facility was compounded by the record-setting $1.25 billion land sale on which it sits.

sections.label: MOH median waiting time data
sections.summary: Data released by MOH suggest the median waiting time could have been almost 24 hours.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Data released by MOH suggest that the median waiting time could have been almost 24 hours.

sections.label: Fear overstretched public health system
sections.summary: The speaker fears such waits are a foretaste of an overstretched public health system operating alongside a lightly regulated private system.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: My fear is that such waits are but a foretaste of what an overstretched public health system, forced to operate alongside a parallel private system with only light regulation, could yield.

sections.label: Enrolled patients consulting other GPs
sections.summary: The question asks whether a patient already enrolled with a family doctor can consult other GPs and still enjoy Healthier SG benefits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: First, can a patient, who has already enrolled with a family doctor, consult other GPs and still enjoy Healthier SG benefits?

sections.label: TCM practitioners in preventive healthcare
sections.summary: The question asks if the Government will review involving TCM practitioners in community preventive healthcare, since acupuncture is offered in restructured hospitals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Will the Government take this opportunity to review how we involve TCM practitioners in community preventive healthcare, especially, since acupuncture is also offered in our restructured hospitals?

sections.label: Speeding up Healthier SG under 60
sections.summary: The question asks whether implementation of Healthier SG can be sped up for residents under 60 years old.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Third, can we speed up the implementation of Healthier SG to residents under 60 years old?

sections.label: Subsidies for ancillary services
sections.summary: Asks whether the Government will subsidise ancillary services to match those at tertiary healthcare institutions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Third, will the cost of ancillary services be subsidised by the Government so that it is on par with those provided by tertiary healthcare institutions?

sections.label: Annual fee beyond CDMP
sections.summary: Asks whether the annual fee for providing care for enrolled patients will extend beyond CDMP conditions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Fifth, will the annual fee for providing care for enrolled patients be extended beyond CDMP conditions?

sections.label: GP end-of-life care planning
sections.summary: Hopes that under Healthier SG, GPs can be incentivised to start end-of-life care planning with patients.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Sixth, I hope that under Healthier SG, GPs can be incentivised to start end-of-life care planning with their patients.

sections.label: Who does Healthier SG screenings
sections.summary: Asks the Ministry to clarify whether Healthier SG screenings are primarily done by GPs or Eldercare Centres.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Can the Ministry clarify whether screenings under Healthier SG are primarily done by GPs or Eldercare Centres (ECs)?

sections.label: Population in Brief report
sections.summary: States that the Government's Population in Brief report was released last week.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The Government's Population in Brief report was released last week.

sections.label: GP distribution private versus public
sections.summary: States that 80% of GPs are in the private sector and 20% in polyclinics and hospitals.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: Eighty percent of our GPs are in the private sector and only 20% of them are in polyclinics and hospitals handling 80% of our population.

sections.label: Senior care centres increase
sections.summary: The speaker notes a growing need for more senior care centres and welcomes MOH plans to increase them.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: We could feel the increasing need for more senior care centres.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: I am delighted to read that MOH has plans to increase these centres.

sections.label: Day care and GPs
sections.summary: The speaker believes lower costs will lead more families to choose day care, and wants GPs and Primary Care Networks involved.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: With more understanding of how senior day care centres work, the lower cost involved, I believe more families will be willing to have their loved ones in day care rather than nursing homes when they are still able to handle.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: We need to get our GPs to come on board to be a coordinator of care for the elderly and the Primary Care Networks (PCN) under Healthier SG to play a bigger role in our elderly care centres.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: We can engage our neighbourhood doctors who know their clients well to educate or refer them to day care facilities.

sections.label: Attracting and retaining centre staff
sections.summary: The speaker asks how to attract, train, support and retain centre staff for expanded Healthier SG roles.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: How can we further attract, train, support and retain the staff of these centres to take on the expanded roles as envisaged by Healthier SG?

sections.label: Training for chronic conditions
sections.summary: The speaker asks what training staff need for chronic conditions and calls for a coordinated strategy.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: What kind of training or qualifications are needed for some of the staff to manage clients with such chronic conditions?

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: Will we see our daycare progressing to handle more chronic conditions?

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: We will need a well-coordinated strategy that takes into account public health, sustainability, resilience, training, trust and our ageing population.

sections.label: Nutri-Grade labelling and lower-sodium salt
sections.summary: New Nutri-Grade labelling and advertising prohibitions apply to prepacked and dispenser beverages from 30 December 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: To reduce the intake of sugar, beverages sold in Singapore in prepacked form and from automatic beverage dispensers will be subject to new Nutri-Grade labelling requirements and advertising prohibitions from 30 December 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Similar measures for freshly prepared beverages will come into effect by end of 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: In fact, supermarket chains FairPrice and Sheng Siong will start selling lower-sodium salt products starting from this week.

sections.label: Vaping in schools
sections.summary: MOH and MOE are addressing vaping in schools, with a vape-free campaign in 2023 for youths and younger adults.

sentences.text: Next year, caregivers will also be able to use HealthHub to help their loved ones enrol to Healthier SG.

sections.label: Healthpoints after first consultation

sentences.speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
sentences.text: You will also receive Healthpoints after enrolling and completing the first consultation with your enrolled family doctor.

sections.label: Healthier SG enrolment age 60

sentences.speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
sentences.text: Enrolment for Healthier SG will start in the second half of 2023 for those aged 60 and above.

sections.label: Healthier SG White Paper turning point
sections.summary: A quote describes the Healthier SG White Paper, which represents a major turning point in public healthcare policy.

sentences.text: This wise and well-known quote is apt to describe the Healthier SG White Paper.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: It also represents a major turning point in our public healthcare policy.

sections.label: Ageing population healthcare expenditure
sections.summary: The increase in public healthcare expenditure can be slowed and the burden on future generations lightened despite a rapidly ageing population.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: First, although we are a rapidly ageing population, the increase in public healthcare expenditure can be slowed down and the burden on future generations will also be lightened.

sections.label: Prevention and people's buy in
sections.summary: Moving Singapore's health focus from treatment to prevention is necessary, but realising the White Paper vision depends on people's genuine buy in.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: To move Singapore's health focus from treatment to prevention is necessary.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: However, in my view, the key to realising the vision of the White Paper lies in getting the people's genuine buy in.

sections.label: Care protocols for GPs

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: In the White Paper, care protocols are mentioned to enhance the consistency of GPs in the care of chronic illnesses.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Can the Government introduce mental health care with the "three highs" care protocols?

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Overall, the intention of the Healthier SG White Paper is clear and should be supported.

sections.label: Publishing multiplier of fees
sections.summary: The speaker said a multiplier of existing charges should be published so consumers know how much more or less expensive their doctor may be relative to the benchmark.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: What I said was that we should publish more of a multiplier of existing charges.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: If anything, I think that we do not need to publish all the fees in doctors offices, per se.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: We should publish it as a matter of course in literature, but rather, we should allow the multiplier of fees to be published so that the consumer is aware of how much more or less expensive their doctor may be relative to the benchmark.

sections.label: MediShield Life price negotiation
sections.summary: The speaker said MediShield Life should be more proactive in negotiating price setting, as it is a prominent insurer.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: What I said instead was that MediShield Life should be a lot more proactive in negotiating for price setting.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: And that is important because MediShield Life is, in fact, one of the more prominent insurers in the existing market.

sections.label: Inactivity health and economic costs
sections.summary: Bach called sport low-cost, high-impact tools, and WHO statistics show inactivity and its healthcare and productivity costs.

sentences.text: International Olympic Committee President Thomas Bach said that "sport and physical activity are the low-cost, high-impact tools for healthy bodies, healthy minds and resilient communities." The World Health Organization statistics show that one in four adults, and four out of five adolescents do not get enough physical activity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Globally, the estimated to cost US$54 billion in direct healthcare and another US$14 billion in lost productivity.

sections.label: Engaging sports community in Healthier SG

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: What are MOH's plans to engage the sports, fitness and wellness community in its Healthier SG strategy?

sections.label: Exercise is Medicine course

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: One such course is Exercise is Medicine, which is a global health initiative managed by the American College of Sports Medicine.

sections.label: White Paper connecting vulnerable groups
sections.summary: The White Paper must connect with Singaporeans of different backgrounds and abilities, including persons with disabilities and the less technologically savvy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The White Paper must be able to connect with Singaporeans from different socio-economic backgrounds, or different physical and cognitive abilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This includes persons with disabilities as well as those who are not technologically savvy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It would be reassuring to hear details on how the Minister has considered these vulnerable groups in MOH's plans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I firmly believe that Healthier SG is a strategy which will support our healthcare workers, by placing a greater responsibility of an individual's health on the individual and also provide access to a wide network of support and expertise bolstered by a robust technology platform.

sections.label: WHO sugar tax research
sections.summary: A WHO-funded report examined sugar tax effects in countries with it and found a 15% decrease in demand for sugared drinks.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: And a few months ago, a research that was funded by the World Health Organization came up with a report that examined the effect of this tax on the countries or regions that have in place this sugar tax.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: And it was found that it decreased demand for sugared drinks by 15%.

sections.label: Sugar tax suggestion
sections.summary: Ms Hazel Poa suggested a sugar tax.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The Member, Ms Hazel Poa, has suggested a sugar tax.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Which is why for MOH, we decided against it – notwithstanding other countries having imposed sugar tax.

sections.label: Sugar consumption reduction achieved

sentences.text: As a result, today – I do not have the data with me – but we are achieving a reduction in sugar consumption as effectively as the UK with labelling and without a sugar tax.

sections.label: Healthier SG affordability measures
sections.summary: Healthier SG will make healthcare more affordable through screening and vaccination subsidies, MediSave co-payment waiver, and a new CHAS drug subsidy tier.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: The Labour Movement is therefore heartened that Healthier SG will help to make healthcare more affordable through: one, subsidies on health screenings and vaccinations; two, waiver of the co-payment requirement when using MediSave for chronic care management; and three, introduction of the new Community Health Assist Scheme (CHAS) drug subsidy tier for a whitelist of chronic disease management drugs to ensure that medications for chronic illnesses are made affordable.

sections.label: Employers mitigating chronic illnesses
sections.summary: Employers must mitigate job-specific chronic illnesses by designing work environments, providing workplace health screenings, and offering healthier eating options.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Employers therefore must do their part to mitigate job-specific chronic illnesses faced by their workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: They can do so in three ways: one, design the work environment to prevent chronic illnesses from forming; two, provide structured health screenings at the workplace, targeting job-specific chronic illnesses; and three, provide healthier eating options within the workplace.

sections.label: Employers including Healthier SG clinics
sections.summary: Employers should work with insurers and third-party administrators to include more Healthier SG clinics on panels and offer screenings and vaccinations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Second, all employers should work with their insurers and third-party administrators to include more Healthier SG clinics on their panels and offer structured health screenings and vaccinations for their workers.

sections.label: Public transport workers plates
sections.summary: More than 100,000 plates have been taken up by public transport workers since the campaign started.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Since the campaign started, more than 100,000 plates have been taken up by our public transport workers.

sections.label: COVID-19 mental health studies
sections.summary: A 2021 Institute of Mental Health study found the COVID-19 pandemic led to a rise in mental health issues in Singapore.

sentences.text: According to a 2021 study by the Institute of Mental Health, the COVID-19 pandemic has led to a rise in mental health issues in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: A 2021 survey by software company Oracle found that nearly seven in 10 residents in Singapore said that 2021 was the most stressful year at work.

sections.label: Improving mental healthcare access

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Could we consider improving access to mental healthcare support to all Singaporeans by increasing the current psychiatrist-to-population ratio to 10 per 100,000 residents, similar to other countries such as the United States and Australia?

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: We should also encourage Singaporeans to have a dedicated counsellor or psychologist, similar to how we are encouraging everyone to have a regular family doctor, to serve as their first point of contact for their mental health.

sections.label: Ageing population and life expectancy
sections.summary: One in four citizens are expected to be aged 65 and above by 2030, up from one in six today.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: One in four citizens are expected to be aged 65 and above by 2030, up from one in six today.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: While our life expectancy is one of the highest in the world at 85 years, our health-adjusted life expectancy is 75 years.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: The proportion of population with high blood pressure has increased, from 20% in 2010 to 32% in 2020, and 26% to 37% for high blood cholesterol.

sections.label: National Steps Challenge participation
sections.summary: Out of those 50 years old and above, 280,000 participate in National Steps Challenge on Healthy 365.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Already, out of those 50 years old and above, 280,000 participate in National Steps Challenge on Healthy 365.

sections.label: Action Plan for Successful Ageing
sections.summary: In 2015, MCA launched the Action Plan for Successful Ageing, covering 70 initiatives across 12 areas.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: In 2015, MCA launched the Action Plan for Successful Ageing, covering 70 initiatives across 12 areas.

sections.label: Day and home care places
sections.summary: Between 2012 and 2020, around 6,000 day care places and 5,500 home care places were added for seniors with a range of care needs.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Between 2012 and 2020, we added around 6,000 day care places and 5,500 home care places to cater to seniors with a range of care needs.

sections.label: Refreshing the Action Plan

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: The MCA is refreshing the Action Plan for Successful Ageing.

sections.label: Action Plan Refresh 3Cs
sections.summary: The Action Plan Refresh will be anchored on Care, Contribution and Connectedness, called the 3Cs.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: The Action Plan Refresh will be anchored on Care, Contribution and Connectedness, or what we call the 3Cs.

sections.label: Community Care Apartments
sections.summary: MOH and MND developed housing-cum-care options, launching the first Community Care Apartments in Bukit Batok and a second in Queenstown in the November 2022 BTO exercise.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: MOH has been working closely with MND to develop new housing-cum-care options to support seniors to age in community.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: We launched our first Community Care Apartments –which are senior-friendly housing integrated with care services – in Bukit Batok last year.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: And we will be launching our second in Queenstown in the November 2022 BTO exercise.

sections.label: Doubling ECs by 2025
sections.summary: Doubling ECs by 2025 is expected to let eight in 10 seniors access activities near their homes, supporting ageing in community.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: When we double our ECs by 2025, we expect eight in 10 seniors to be able to access these activities near their homes.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: All these efforts, together with Healthier SG’s emphasis on preventive care, lay a strong foundation for seniors to age in community, a major reform of our aged care ecosystem.

sections.label: Woodlands Health Campus utilisation trends
sections.summary: Woodlands Health Campus utilisation trends show 20% of patients use up to 80% of healthcare cost, often shunning GPs and ending in A&E.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In fact, Woodlands Health Campus' utilisation trends show that 20% of patients use up to 80% of healthcare cost.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Often, these are the people who will shun visiting the GP when they are sick because they cannot afford to pay the cash even after subsidies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: They end up getting into A&E when their conditions get too severe.

sections.label: Yishun Health Wellness Kampung outreach
sections.summary: Yishun Health community outreach teams' Wellness Kampung efforts show peers influencing peers through share and care activities using residents' assets.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Yet, in the example of the Yishun Health community outreach teams' Wellness Kampung efforts, we see how peers can influence peers to see that, "If you can, maybe I can too." Such share and care activities harness the power of the community and the assets and strengths from amongst residents themselves to initiate activities that provide positive influence and share their own knowledge with one another.

sections.label: MOH-funded PA community health team
sections.summary: The speaker calls for MOH to lead and fund a dedicated PA community health team trained in asset-based community development with Yishun Health.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Specifically, I call for MOH to lead and to help fund a dedicated community health team within PA to train specifically personnel in asset-based community development in collaboration with Yishun Health's community outreach team as well as other community partners who are well-versed and familiar with the A-B-C-D model.

sections.label: Nee Soon neighbour care pilot
sections.summary: In Nee Soon, the speaker is piloting an experiment with Yishun Health to tap neighbours to help discharge patients lacking home care.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In Nee Soon, I am now piloting an experiment with Yishun Health to explore tapping on neighbours to help so that the hospital can readily discharge patients who are ready to be discharged but may not have people at home to care for them.

sections.label: Expanding Community Capability Trust funding
sections.summary: The speaker suggests expanding the Community Capability Trust with MOH funding for social enterprises and tax deductions for impact investors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: One, it is possible to look into expanding the Community Capability Trust with specific funding injections from MOH to invest in social enterprises that provide such capability building services for the community.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This is really to help them during their startup stage.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We can also consider providing Government tax deduction benefits to impact investors who invest in early stage social enterprises that provide similar services in the same way that it incentivises donations to Institutions of Public Character (IPCs) because after all, if more people can be harnessed and built in their capability to care in the neighbourhoods, then we all can hopefully pay less taxes because of institutional healthcare costs.

sections.label: Healthier SG doctor patient limits
sections.summary: The speaker asks the maximum number of patients each family doctor can accept and the criteria for accepting or rejecting patients under Healthier SG.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: As such, I would like to ask what is maximum number of patients each family doctor can accept?

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: What is the set of criteria which doctors can use to decide whether to accept or reject existing and new patients under Healthier SG?

sections.label: GP clinic family doctor registration
sections.summary: A GP asks if family doctors must join the Primary Care Network; the Healthier SG White Paper requires each GP clinic to have one family doctor registered as a family physician within seven years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: Meanwhile, one GP, who is an owner-doctor running his own clinic has requested me to ask if it is compulsory for all family doctors to join the Primary Care Network (PCN).

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: Referring to page 42 of the Healthier SG White Paper, it states that each GP clinic must have at least one family doctor to be registered as a family physician within seven years of the launch of Healthier SG.

sections.label: Healthier SG GP costs
sections.summary: Minister Ong indicated about $1 billion over three to four years for IT support and one-off costs to bring GPs on board Healthier SG, with recurring costs of $400 million a year including GP service fees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: Minister Ong had indicated that it would cost about $1 billion over the next three to four years for IT support and other one-off costs to bring the GPs on board Healthier SG.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: At the same time, the recurring cost of running Healthier SG will amount to $400 million a year, including the service fee for the GPs.

sections.label: Reducing years in ill health
sections.summary: Dr Chuang said people want a fuller life rather than a longer one; Singaporeans' life expectancy is close to 85 years but they spend more than 10 years in ill health, which Healthier SG hopes to reduce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: Dr Chuang said, “People want to live a fuller live, rather than a longer life.” “People want to live a fuller live, rather than a longer life.” Currently, Singaporeans' life expectancy is close to 85 years but they spend more than 10 years in ill health.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: With Healthier SG, we hope to reduce the number of years spent in ill health.

sections.label: TCM integration into Healthier SG
sections.summary: Minister Ong replied that TCM practitioners are important stakeholders but, unlike Western doctors, are not tightly regulated by MOH, so the same approach cannot be taken.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In July this year, I asked the Minister for Health in a written Parliamentary Question how TCM practitioners would be integrated into the Ministry's Healthier SG plans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Minister Ong replied and I quote: "Traditional Chinese Medicine practitioners are important stakeholders, especially given their emphasis on holistic and long-term care.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, unlike Western doctors, Traditional Chinese Medicine practitioners are not tightly regulated by MOH.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The standard of care delivery varies widely and we will therefore not be able to take the same approach as we have taken for Western doctors." This reply is nonetheless not inconsistent with the Minister's public comments in December 2021 where Minister was quoted as recognising the benefits of TCM in fighting chronic diseases.

sections.label: Extending MediSave to TCM
sections.summary: A suggestion for the Government to consider extending MediSave use for more TCM procedures and alternative therapies proven in managing general health and preventing chronic diseases, including certified TCM practitioners in their clinics outside public healthcare institutions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To this end, Sir, my first suggestion is for the Government to consider extending the use of MediSave for more TCM procedures and alternative therapies that have a proven role in the management of one's general health and, more pertinently, in the prevention of chronic diseases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This expansion should also see the inclusion of certified TCM practitioners who can be allowed to offer such approved procedures in their TCM clinics outside public healthcare institutions.

sections.label: Fybogel versus psyllium husk cost
sections.summary: Fybogel for constipation can cost around $20 on the shelf without subsidies, while psyllium husk with similar benefits can be bought from Little India and NTUC supermarkets at under $3.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For example, Fybogel, which is commonly dispensed for constipation, can cost around $20 on the shelf without subsidies, whereas psyllium husk, which confers similar, if not identical, benefits, can be purchased from Little India and even NTUC supermarkets at under $3.

sections.label: TCM rehabilitation and physiotherapy
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Ministry would consider TCM practitioners undertaking rehabilitation or physiotherapy at TCM clinics.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In this light, would the Ministry consider whether there is scope for such rehabilitation or physiotherapy to be undertaken at TCM clinics by TCM practitioners?

sections.label: Subsidising TCM practitioners under Healthier SG
sections.summary: The passage states MOH should tap TCM practitioners to share healthy living tips and preventive healthcare, and not rule out subsidising them under Healthier SG criteria.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: MOH should tap on them to help share healthy living tips and preventive healthcare strategies, not just to our seniors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And MOH should not rule out subsidising TCM practitioners in this endeavour, subject to their contributions towards objective criteria under Healthier SG.

sections.label: Speeches on TCM and Healthier SG

sentences.text: I was going to call Mr Henry Kwek.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: I am glad that he read my Parliamentary answer on TCM and also my December 2021 speech on TCM.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: I just wonder, last month, I gave two more speeches about TCM and Healthier SG.

sections.label: Self-funded eldercare centre in Ang Mo Kio
sections.summary: The passage states Dementia Singapore and volunteers set up a self-funded eldercare centre within Block 115 in Ang Mo Kio.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: A few years ago, Dementia Singapore and my volunteers set up a self-funded eldercare centre from scratch within Block 115 in Ang Mo Kio.

sections.label: More eldercare centres under Healthier SG
sections.summary: The passage states volunteers were thrilled that under Healthier SG, MOH will set up more eldercare centres integrating community programmes with health.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: He has learnt to come to terms with his disability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Now, given what we have seen, my volunteers and I are, of course, thrilled when we heard that under Healthier SG, MOH will set up many more eldercare centres that integrate community programmes with health.

sections.label: Longevity research and MOH plan
sections.summary: The passage describes attending Singapore's first longevity research conference and asks MOH to sketch out its emerging plan for healthy longevity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Last month, I was delighted to attend and join in a panel at Singapore's first longevity research conference where Deputy Prime Minister Heng Swee Keat launched NUHS' Centre for Healthy Longevity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Yes, I understand the science is still developing, but it will be wonderful if MOH can sketch out what our emerging plan is because healthy longevity can have a profound impact because Singapore can be the first country to systematically translate longevity research into practical intervention for all.

sections.label: Investing in preventive health
sections.summary: A speaker hopes healthcare leaders boldly invest resources and imagination in preventive health despite instincts to spend most on the sick.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Thirdly, I hope that our healthcare leaders boldly invest resources and imagination in preventive health, even though our natural instincts are to spend the most to care for the sick.

sections.label: MOH oversight of preventive spending
sections.summary: A speaker hopes MOH keeps close tabs that regional health systems spend enough on preventive care and refines the funding model over time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: But I do hope that MOH can keep close tabs to ensure that all regional health systems spend enough on preventive care.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: And that over time, MOH can refine the funding model to factor in differing age distribution, social economic status across different healthcare clusters.

sections.label: Kebun Baru healthy longevity plan
sections.summary: Kebun Baru has started creating a local action plan for healthy longevity, hoping to partner with NHG on it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: In fact, we have started creating our Kebun Baru local action plan for healthy longevity, that we hope to partner with NHG on.

sections.label: Longevity interventions and micro-jobs
sections.summary: They will reach out to the Centre for Healthy Longevity so residents benefit from longevity interventions, and power local efforts with micro-jobs for healthy seniors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: We will reach out to the Centre for Healthy Longevity, so that our residents can benefit from longevity interventions as soon as possible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: And lastly, we will power some of these local efforts with micro-jobs for our healthy seniors.

sections.label: Twelve primary care protocols
sections.summary: Twelve care protocols were developed with primary care teams for screening, vaccination and managing chronic conditions, with more protocols to come.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Several Members of this House have also raised similar concerns and provided suggestions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: We have worked with primary care teams to develop 12 care protocols.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: These will provide clarity and consistent processes for the GPs and the clusters who will support them.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: The protocols are on providing screening and vaccination, and managing common chronic conditions like diabetes, hypertension and lipid disorders.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: This will be a multi-year effort and we will continue to develop more care protocols, such as for mental and dental health.

sections.label: Growing family physician pool
sections.summary: In response to questions on personnel and overseas Singaporean healthcare workers, the pool of family physicians is being grown toward 3,500 by 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: To Mr Xie Yao Quan and Ms He Ting Ru's questions on personnel and overseas Singaporeans who are healthcare workers, we are actively growing our pool of family physicians to meet our target of 3,500 by 2030.

sections.label: Overseas trained Singaporean doctors returning
sections.summary: About 200 overseas trained Singaporean doctors return each year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Overall, about 200 overseas trained Singaporean doctors come back every year.

sections.label: Family physician per clinic
sections.summary: The intent is for all participating clinics to have at least one family physician per clinic.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: The intent is for all participating clinics to have at least one family physician per clinic.

sections.label: GP IT system transition support
sections.summary: GPs get one year from Healthier SG's launch to adjust to a compatible IT system, plus a one-off IT support grant.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: We know that it is not easy for GPs to upgrade to an IT system that is Healthier SG compatible, and they will have one year from the launch of Healthier SG to adjust.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: We will also provide a one-off IT support grant to support this transition.

sections.label: Health Information Bill safeguards
sections.summary: A 2023 Health Information Bill will govern safe collection, use and sharing of health data, with access limited to authorised personnel.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: We will continue to implement safeguards to balance patients' need for privacy and to ensure that the correct healthcare providers are able to access critical information necessary to provide care to patients.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: We will introduce new legislation, the Health Information Bill, in 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: This Bill will facilitate the proper collection, use and sharing of health data among healthcare providers in a safe and secure manner.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Only authorised personnel will be allowed to access the data, which will be limited to what is necessary for their work.

sections.label: FIT screening for ages 50 and above
sections.summary: For those aged 50 and above, a 2-day Faecal Immunochemical Test is used for colorectal cancer.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: One example is what we are doing for those aged 50 and above, such as with the 2-day Faecal Immunochemical Test (FIT) which is for colorectal cancer.

sections.label: Community mental health services access
sections.summary: Community Outreach Teams were developed, addiction services extended to more hospitals, over 390 GP partners trained, and an interagency taskforce convened.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: To improve access to community mental health services, we developed Community Outreach Teams (CREST).

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: The National Addictions Management Service at IMH will be extended to other hospitals, including Changi General Hospital and National University Hospital, to make the services more accessible.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: As of March 2022, there were over 390 GP partners trained to care for persons with mental health conditions in the community.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: We have convened the Interagency Taskforce on Mental Health & Well-being with members from over 30 organisations.

sections.label: TCM self-regulation and workgroups
sections.summary: MOH and the TCM community established two workgroups on clinical training and career development, and the TCM Board Chairman succession plan was finalised.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: While we work that out, in the mean time, we encourage TCM practitioners to continue to do what you are good at, advise the patients to take care of their health, pick up good habits, live healthily and take care of their health holistically.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: But like I said in my Parliamentary reply, TCM is self-regulated, with varying standards of practice.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: So, over the last year, MOH and the TCM community have established two workgroups.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: They work on issues such as enhancing TCM clinical training and improving career development.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: And once completed, this can be a basis to explore how to involve TCM in support of Healthier SG.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: I think self-regulation for something that is traditional and cultural, would be more appropriate.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: We have recently also finalised the succession plan of the Chairman of the TCM Board.

sections.label: Incoming TCM Board Chairman
sections.summary: The incoming Chairman of the TCM Board will be Dr Teo Ho Pin.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The incoming Chairman will be Dr Teo Ho Pin, another familiar colleague of ours.

sections.label: Limits on GP resident enrolment
sections.summary: GPs will be asked to set a limit on the number of residents they can enrol.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: I tried to explain some of this in my opening speech that we will try our best to manage this.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: We will ask GPs to set a limit on number of residents they can enrol.

sections.label: Drug price parity
sections.summary: Drug price parity is an important concern raised by residents, especially for the lower income.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: But parity of drug prices is an important concern, told to us by many residents when we did our consultation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: And we will try our best to make sure there is drug price parity, especially for the lower income.

sections.label: Cardiac arrest survival and readmissions
sections.summary: Community measures for out-of-hospital cardiac arrests raised survival from 2% to 22%, and early review cut 30-day re-admissions from 14.3% to 9.6%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: One, all the community measures taken to help resuscitate out-of-hospital cardiac arrests by making defibrillators available in the community, training members of the public to perform CPR, alerting them through apps, that there is a cardiac arrest nearby.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: And so far, the survival rate of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest has improved by 10 times – 2% to 22% over the years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The idea is to review the patient's condition early within two weeks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: This has resulted in a reduction of the 30-day re-admission rate from 14.3% to 9.6%.

sections.label: Capitation-based cluster budgets
sections.summary: At the healthcare cluster level, the basis of calculating budgets was changed to be capitation-based.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: At the healthcare cluster level, we have changed the basis of calculating their budgets to be capitation-based.

sections.label: MOH internal parameters
sections.summary: The speaker says it is better to keep this as internal parameters within MOH for now.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: For now, I think it is better we keep this as internal parameters within MOH.

sections.label: Healthcare workforce growth to 2030
sections.summary: Nurses, allied health professionals and support care staff number about 58,000 now and MOH estimates growth to 82,000 in 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The key challenge is to have sufficient nurses, allied health professionals and support care staff to operate hospitals, clinics and also eldercare centres.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: These few groups number about 58,000 now and MOH estimates that this will need to grow to 82,000 in 2030 – 58,000 to 82,000 from now to 2030.

sections.label: Nursing student intake increase
sections.summary: Nursing student intake rose from about 1,500 a year ten years ago to 2,100 now, with plans to increase to 2,300.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Ten years ago, ITE, Polytechnics and Universities in Singapore took in about 1,500 nursing students a year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Now, this has gone up to 2,100 and we are trying to increase it further to 2,300 in the next couple of years.

sections.label: Foreign nurse attrition rise
sections.summary: Attrition of foreign nurses rose from about 8.9% in normal years to 14.8% in 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: What has gone up is the attrition of foreign nurses – from about 8.9% in normal years to 14.8% in 2021.

sections.label: Ageing population and workforce impact
sections.summary: By 2030 about one in four Singaporeans will be 65 and above, up from one in six today, affecting companies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: By 2030, one in four Singaporeans or thereabouts will be 65 and above, up from one in six today.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The number translates into real impact on our lives and we have yet to feel the full brunt of it.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: For companies, you will face a shortage of workers, requiring you to move into automation, adopt less manpower-intensive business models while using foreign workers judiciously.

sections.label: Ageing and disease burden premise
sections.summary: The speaker states ageing may be inexorable but rapid escalation of disease burden and suffering need not be a given.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Our basic premise must be this – ageing may be an inexorable trend but a rapid escalation of disease burden and suffering need not be a given.

sections.label: Nursing home bed expansion
sections.summary: Nursing homes cannot be the mainstream solution to ageing, though beds are growing from 16,200 now to 31,000 in 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: But nursing homes are not and cannot be the mainstream solution to ageing.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: We are building nursing homes very quickly, from 16,200 beds now, to 31,000 beds in 2030.

sections.label: Loneliness and senior independence
sections.summary: A volunteer-run effort helps seniors, loneliness harms health like 15 cigarettes daily, and 97% of seniors above 65 live independently or with help.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: It is not run on a big budget, a lot of passionate volunteers, we all know who got involved, but it is doing such heavy lifting and making such a huge difference to the seniors living in that block.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: I came across this piece of research, which estimated that the health impact of loneliness for a senior is equivalent to smoking 15 cigarettes a day.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: We estimate that today, 97% of our seniors above 65 can either live independently or with some help in the community.

sections.label: Eldercare Centres in existing spaces
sections.summary: MOH is expanding Eldercare Centres to activate existing spaces and create shared spaces and social networks for seniors.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: We did not specifically build them as infrastructure to support ageing, but they are extremely valuable in our ageing society.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: And that is why MOH is rapidly expanding our network of Eldercare Centres to activate these existing spaces and create more shared spaces and social networks for seniors.

sections.label: Ageing in communities reform
sections.summary: Ageing in communities will be the next major area of change and reform in healthcare.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Ageing in communities will be the next major area of change and reform in healthcare that we need to work on.

sections.label: Healthier SG and aged care
sections.summary: Healthier SG reforms the public health system, empowers individuals to choose health, and lays the foundation for the aged care system.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Healthier SG is a key effort to activate and reform the public health system, empower individuals to choose health and lay the foundation for the aged care system I spoke about.

sections.label: Endorsing Healthier SG transformation
sections.summary: Population ageing is an urgent test, and support is sought to endorse Healthier SG as the basis to transform healthcare for long healthy lives.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: All societies, at some point, will have to confront population ageing.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: It is an urgent and stern test, and some societies end up with bankrupted healthcare systems or let healthcare cripple their society and economy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: We have the resources, ability, organisation and determination to do this.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: I seek the support of this House and of the people of Singapore to endorse this Healthier SG effort as the basis to transform our healthcare system, so as to strive towards the vision of long and healthy lives for Singaporeans.

sections.label: Reducing outpatient visits for caregivers
sections.summary: An MP asks if the Ministry can reduce visits by giving care providers time to coordinate care for frail patients with many medical issues.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: In a Parliamentary Question earlier this year that I asked, and which I raised in Committee of Supply, there are Singaporeans today who may have 20 or even 30 outpatient visits in a single year, each of these visits poses challenges for the caregivers, especially caregivers who may be daily rated and cannot get time-off from their employer.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: As part of Healthier SG and strengthening coordination of care, can the Ministry also help look at ways to reduce the number of visits, by giving care providers, doctors and healthcare workers additional time and bandwidth, to help further coordinate and streamline the care for such patients who face frailty and many medical issues?

sections.label: Breakdown of $1 billion funding
sections.summary: The Minister lists what the slightly over $1 billion covers and mentions recurrent expenses of about $400 million a year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I have one clarification for the Minister for Health.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: I do not have the numbers with me but of the $1 billion, slightly over $1 billion, there is a chunk for the central IT system, there is a chunk to upgrade the capabilities and IT capabilities of GPs, there is a chunk to upgrade or build up capabilities within the clusters in order to be regional health managers, there is a chunk to do a one-time ramp up of social activities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So, they all add up to over $1 billion .

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: But what the Member did not ask is also, in terms of recurrent, I did mention recurrent expenses of about $400 million a year.

sections.label: MediSave co-payment and withdrawal limit
sections.summary: An MP asks whether patients can use MediSave for co-payment and whether the annual withdrawal limit still applies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: But I also do not think that we should start out such a major initiative without any target set.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And lastly, the Healthier SG White Paper said that MOH will waive the requirement for residents to co-pay part of their bills in cash.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Can I clarify that patients will be able to use MediSave to make that co-payment?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And will that still be subject to the annual withdrawal limit?

sections.label: Minister on $400 million spending
sections.summary: The Minister says the $400 million is first to subsidise residents for health screening and health points.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Ms Hazel Poa asked a question but she is actually making a statement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: She is saying that Healthier SG, $400 million to spend, as I just answered, $400 million is, first, to subsidise residents for health screening, health points and all that.
